review:
I always find it fascinating when a movie mixes live-action and animation in a cohesive way, and to me, Coyote vs. Acme does this really well. They mix animated characters from Looney Tunes and live-action characters so well in that world that, throughout the film, it makes the suspension of disbelief on that really easy, leaving us more time to appreciate it and laugh at some comical parts.

But animated characters done well in a live-action are not the only positive aspect of the film. The story, which is based on a satirical article from a 1990 issue of The New Yorker, is a well constructed and clever one, although the pace of it seems a bit off at times. The plot revolves around Wile E. Coyote, who, after failing once again to catch the Road runner due to his Acme-produced gadgets malfunctioning, as often happens to him, decides to hire a law firm specialized in small cases brought by animated characters against Acme. The issue is, this firm usually focus only on small cases, and is not used to one that is the size of many years of comedic failures. And so, this is what brings the human cast and animated characters together to try and win the case against Acme.

If you liked classic cartoons with Wile E. Coyote and the Road Runner, chances are this movie will be a good time for you, providing some laughs and even some newfound compassion for these characters.
